## Activity 1: The Big Reveal — Lab A vs Lab B (20 min)

### What You Didn't Know

There was a **hidden manipulation** in the memory task:

- **Lab A** memorised **abstract** words: justice, freedom, wisdom...
- **Lab B** memorised **concrete** words: chair, river, mountain...

Let's see if it made a difference!


::: {.cell layout-align="center"}
::: {.cell-output-display}
![](activity_files/figure-html/lab-comparison-1.png){fig-align='center' width=672}
:::
:::


### The Numbers

::: {.cell-output-display}

|Lab A
(Abstract) |  8| 6.00| 1.51|   3|   8|

### Design Detective Questions

Now identify the design elements:

**1. What did the researcher MANIPULATE?**

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value='answer'>Word type (abstract vs concrete)</option><option value=''>Number of words</option><option value=''>Time allowed</option><option value=''>Nothing was manipulated</option></select>

**2. What variable is this called?**

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value='answer'>Independent Variable (IV)</option><option value=''>Dependent Variable (DV)</option><option value=''>Control Variable</option><option value=''>Confounding Variable</option></select>

**3. What did the researcher MEASURE?**

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>Word type</option><option value='answer'>Number of words recalled</option><option value=''>Time to recall</option><option value=''>Participant happiness</option></select>

**4. What variable is this called?**

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>Independent Variable (IV)</option><option value='answer'>Dependent Variable (DV)</option><option value=''>Control Variable</option><option value=''>Confounding Variable</option></select>

**5. Were the SAME people in both labs, or DIFFERENT people?**

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>Same people in both labs</option><option value='answer'>Different people in each lab</option></select>

**6. What type of design is this?**

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value='answer'>Between-subjects</option><option value=''>Within-subjects</option><option value=''>Correlational</option><option value=''>Matched pairs</option></select>

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Check Your Understanding

- **IV** = Word type (abstract vs concrete) — this was manipulated
- **DV** = Words recalled — this was measured
- **Design** = Between-subjects — different people in Lab A vs Lab B
- You were in ONE lab only, not both!
:::

## Activity 2: Same Person, Different Conditions (20 min)

### Pre-Post Mood

You rated your mood BEFORE and AFTER the session. Let's see the change!

![](activity_files/figure-html/mood-change-1.png){fig-align='center' width=672}

:::


**The faint lines connect the SAME PERSON.** This is what makes it a within-subjects design!


::: {.cell}

Table: Mood Ratings Before and After

|:------|----:|----:|--:|

|After  |  6.5| 1.96| 10|

### Design Detective Questions

**1. Were SAME people measured at both time points, or DIFFERENT people?**

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value='answer'>Same people at both time points</option><option value=''>Different people at each time point</option></select>

**2. What type of design is this?**

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>Between-subjects</option><option value='answer'>Within-subjects</option><option value=''>Correlational</option><option value=''>Matched pairs</option></select>

**3. What is the IV?**

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value='answer'>Time (before vs after)</option><option value=''>Mood rating</option><option value=''>Participant ID</option><option value=''>No IV</option></select>

**4. What is the DV?**

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>Time</option><option value='answer'>Mood rating</option><option value=''>Participant ID</option><option value=''>Change score</option></select>

**5. Why is within-subjects design considered "powerful"?**

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>More participants</option><option value='answer'>Each person is their own control</option><option value=''>Easier to run</option><option value=''>No IV needed</option></select>

::: {.callout-note}
## The Key Insight
In the graph above, the lines connect the same person before and after. By comparing each person to THEMSELVES, we control for all individual differences (age, personality, baseline mood, etc.).
:::

## Activity 3: Descriptive Statistics Practice (30 min)

### Understanding Mean and SD

Look at these two groups with the SAME MEAN but different spreads:


::: {.cell layout-align="center"}
::: {.cell-output-display}
![](activity_files/figure-html/spread-demo-1.png){fig-align='center' width=672}
:::
:::


**The mean alone doesn't tell the whole story!**

**Which group shows more VARIABILITY?**

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>Group A (Clustered)</option><option value='answer'>Group B (Spread Out)</option><option value=''>They're the same</option><option value=''>Can't tell</option></select>

**Which group has the LARGER standard deviation?**

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>Group A (Clustered)</option><option value='answer'>Group B (Spread Out)</option><option value=''>They're the same</option><option value=''>Can't tell</option></select>

---

### Reading R Output

Here's what R produces when we ask for descriptive statistics:


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code  code-fold="false"}
# A sample of memory scores
scores <- c(6, 8, 5, 7, 9, 6, 7, 8)

# Get descriptive statistics
mean(scores)
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
[1] 7
```


:::

```{.r .cell-code  code-fold="false"}
sd(scores)
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
[1] 1.309307
```


:::

```{.r .cell-code  code-fold="false"}
summary(scores)
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
   Min. 1st Qu.  Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max. 
      5       6       7       7       8       9 
```


:::
:::


**Reading the output above:**

**1. What is the mean of these scores?**

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>6</option><option value=''>6.5</option><option value='answer'>7</option><option value=''>7.5</option></select>

**2. What is the standard deviation (rounded to 1 decimal)?**

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>0.5</option><option value=''>1.0</option><option value='answer'>1.2</option><option value=''>2.0</option></select>

**3. In the `summary()` output, what does "Min." tell you?**

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value='answer'>The lowest score in the data</option><option value=''>The average score</option><option value=''>The most common score</option><option value=''>The middle score</option></select>

**4. What does "Median" tell you?**

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>The lowest score</option><option value=''>The highest score</option><option value='answer'>The middle value when data is ordered</option><option value=''>The most common score</option></select>

::: {.callout-tip}
## Reading R Output
The key functions for descriptive statistics:

- `mean()` gives you the average
- `sd()` gives you the standard deviation
- `summary()` gives you Min, Quartiles, Median, Mean, Max — a complete picture!
:::

True or False: A larger SD means scores are MORE spread out. <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value='answer'>TRUE</option><option value=''>FALSE</option></select>

True or False: A SD of 0 would mean everyone got the exact same score. <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value='answer'>TRUE</option><option value=''>FALSE</option></select>

Looking at the table above:

**Which lab had the higher mean recall?**

::: {.cell}

:::


**Is the difference between means (about 0.3 words) large or small compared to the SD (about 2)?**

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value='answer'>About the same size as the SD</option><option value=''>Much larger than the SD</option><option value=''>Much smaller than the SD</option></select>

::: {.callout-important}
## The Key Insight
A difference between means only matters if it's **big relative to the spread (SD)**.

- **Signal** = difference between means
- **Noise** = variability within groups (SD)

Is the signal bigger than the noise?

## Activity 4: Hypothesis Writing Practice (20 min)

### Writing Hypotheses for the Memory Experiment

**The experimental hypothesis (H₁)** predicts there WILL be an effect.

**The null hypothesis (H₀)** predicts there will be NO effect.

For the Lab A vs Lab B memory comparison:

**Which is a correct EXPERIMENTAL hypothesis?**

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value='answer'>Concrete words will be recalled better than abstract words</option><option value=''>There will be no difference between word types</option><option value=''>Word type cannot affect memory</option><option value=''>All participants will recall 5 words</option></select>

**Which is a correct NULL hypothesis?**

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>Concrete words will be recalled better</option><option value=''>Abstract words will be recalled better</option><option value='answer'>There will be no difference in recall between word types</option><option value=''>Memory doesn't exist</option></select>

---

### One-tailed vs Two-tailed

**One-tailed**: Predicts the DIRECTION ("Group A will be HIGHER than Group B")

**Two-tailed**: Predicts a difference but NOT the direction ("Groups will DIFFER")

**"Concrete words will be easier to remember than abstract words" is:**

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value='answer'>One-tailed (predicts direction)</option><option value=''>Two-tailed (no direction)</option><option value=''>Null hypothesis</option><option value=''>Not a hypothesis</option></select>

**"Word type will affect memory" is:**

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>One-tailed (predicts direction)</option><option value='answer'>Two-tailed (no direction)</option><option value=''>Null hypothesis</option><option value=''>Not a hypothesis</option></select>

---

### Write Your Own

For the pre-post mood comparison, which hypothesis is correctly written?

**One-tailed hypothesis:**

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value='answer'>Mood ratings will be higher after the session than before</option><option value=''>Mood ratings will change after the session</option><option value=''>There will be no change in mood</option><option value=''>Mood cannot be measured</option></select>

**Two-tailed hypothesis:**

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>Mood will improve after the session</option><option value='answer'>Mood ratings will differ between before and after the session</option><option value=''>There will be no change in mood</option><option value=''>Mood will decrease</option></select>

## Activity 5: MCQ Practice (20 min)

::: {.webex-check .webex-box}

### Investigation 1: Throwing Accuracy

Students threw balls with their dominant hand (10 throws) and their non-dominant hand (5 throws). We measured accuracy (% successful throws).

**1. Design type:**

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>Between-subjects</option><option value='answer'>Within-subjects</option><option value=''>Correlational</option></select>

**2. Why is this within-subjects?**

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>Different people used different hands</option><option value='answer'>The same person threw with BOTH hands</option><option value=''>Hands were randomly assigned</option></select>

**3. What is the IV?**

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value='answer'>Hand used (dominant vs non-dominant)</option><option value=''>Throwing accuracy</option><option value=''>Number of throws</option><option value=''>No IV</option></select>

**4. What is the DV?**

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>Hand used</option><option value='answer'>Throwing accuracy (%)</option><option value=''>Number of throws</option><option value=''>Participant age</option></select>
:::

::: {.webex-check .webex-box}

### Investigation 2: Self-Rating vs Performance

Before throwing, students rated how good they thought they'd be (1-10). We then measured their actual accuracy.

**1. Design type:**

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>Between-subjects</option><option value=''>Within-subjects</option><option value='answer'>Correlational</option></select>

**2. Is there an IV?**

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>Yes - self-rating</option><option value=''>Yes - actual accuracy</option><option value='answer'>No - neither variable was manipulated</option></select>

**3. Why can't we say self-rating CAUSES good performance?**

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>Sample too small</option><option value=''>Wrong test</option><option value='answer'>No manipulation means no causal claim</option></select>
:::

::: {.webex-check .webex-box}

### Investigation 3: Sixth Sense

Students tried to detect if someone was staring at them (6 trials). If just guessing, you'd expect 3/6 (50%) correct.

**1. If someone got 5/6 correct, does that PROVE they have a sixth sense?**

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>TRUE</option><option value='answer'>FALSE</option></select>

**2. Why not?**

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>5/6 is impossible</option><option value='answer'>Some people will get 5/6 just by luck</option><option value=''>The experiment was flawed</option><option value=''>Sixth sense doesn't exist</option></select>

**3. What would 50% accuracy suggest?**

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>They definitely have a sixth sense</option><option value=''>They definitely don't have a sixth sense</option><option value='answer'>Performance at chance level - just guessing</option></select>
:::

## Summary

::: {.callout-important}
## Key Takeaways

**Design Types:**

- **Between-subjects** = Different people in each condition (Lab A vs Lab B)
- **Within-subjects** = Same people in all conditions (Pre vs Post mood)
- **Correlational** = No manipulation, measuring relationships (Self-rating vs accuracy)

**Variables:**

- **IV** = What the researcher manipulates (word type, time)
- **DV** = What the researcher measures (recall, mood rating)
- Correlational designs have **NO IV**

**Descriptive Statistics:**

- **Mean** = Average value
- **SD** = How spread out values are
- A difference between means matters if it's **big relative to the SD**
:::
